data.name: Badeed
data.gender_notes: Badeed is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'daada', meaning to be quick, swift, or rapid. In Islamic history, Badeed is the name of a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) who was known for his swiftness and agility. The name Badeed carries the meaning “Quick, Swift, Rapid” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Badeed usually hope their child will grow to embody quick, swift, rapid and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the idea of being swift and responsive to the will of Allah.
data.etymology: Badeed belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Quick, Swift, Rapid.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Badeed total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: بديد
in_arabic.meaning: اسم بمعنى بعيد أو شخص في مكان بعيد
in_arabic.long_meaning: بديد هو اسم مشتق من الجذر 'بدد' الذي يعني التباعد أو الابتعاد. في اللغة العربية، يوصف الشخص بأنه بديد إذا كان بعيدًا عن مكان أو شخص ما. ويرتبط هذا الاسم بمعنى الابتعاد أو التباعد، سواء كان ذلك في المكان أو في العلاقات. وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم ذكر لفظة 'بدد' في سياقات مختلفة، منها قوله تعالى: 'وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا' (الإسراء: 36)، حيث يشير إلى عدم اتباع الظن أو الشك دون دليل.

in_urdu.name: بدید
in_urdu.meaning: نام کا مطلب دور یا الگ تھوڑا سا شخص
in_urdu.long_meaning: بدید ایک نام ہے جو عربی جڑ 'بدد' سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے دور ہونا یا الگ ہونا۔ اردو میں، اس نام کا تعلق اس خیال سے ہے کہ کوئی شخص جسمانی یا نفسیاتی طور پر دور ہو۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی روایت میں استعمال ہوتا ہے، جہاں اس کا انتخاب اس کی خوبصورت معنی اور روحانی گہرائی کے لئے کیا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: बदीद
in_hindi.meaning: नाम का अर्थ है दूर या अलग
in_hindi.long_meaning: बदीद एक नाम है जो अरबी मूल से निकला है, जिसका अर्थ है 'दूर' या 'अलग'। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में उपयोग किया जाता है, जहां इसे इसकी सुंदर अर्थ और आध्यात्मिक गहराई के लिए चुना जाता है। यह नाम व्यक्ति की विशेषताओं और उनके चरित्र को दर्शाने के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: بديد
in_pashto.meaning: د نوم مطلب دی لرې يا جلا شوی
in_pashto.long_meaning: بديد د يو نوم څخه مشتق دی، چې مانا يې دى لرې يا جلا شوی. په پښتو کې، دا نوم د افغان او پښتن مسلمانانو دوديز ارزښتونو سره تړاو لري، او د يو چا د ځانګړتیاوو او کرکټر د څرګندولو لپاره کارول کېږي.

in_english.name: Badeed
in_english.long_meaning: Badeed is an Arabic-originated name that signifies 'far' or 'distant'. Etymologically derived from the root 'b-d-d', which connotes the idea of separation or distance. In Islamic tradition, this name holds spiritual significance, symbolizing someone who might be physically or metaphorically distant. Historically, the term has been used in various Quranic contexts to denote distance or dispersion. The name Badeed is chosen for its profound meaning and cultural importance across Muslim communities worldwide.

historical_references.reference: The Battle of Badr was a significant early military victory for Muhammad and the Muslims, occurring in 624 AD. This battle signified a turning point in the early Islamic history, as it established the Muslims as a military force to be reckoned with, and allowed them to gain control of the major trade routes.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history, military victory for Muhammad and Muslims

historical_references.reference: The city of Badee'a (or Badee'ah) was a major center of trade and agriculture during the pre-Islamic period, situated on the eastern bank of the Euphrates River. It was an important stop for caravans traveling between the Levant and Mesopotamia. During the early Islamic conquests, the city was seized by Islamic forces led by Khalid ibn al-Walid in 633 AD, marking the expanding reach of the Muslim empire.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic conquests, Islamic forces led by Khalid ibn al-Walid
